learnings: Include specific names, institutions, or countries in titles (e.g., Gupta Family, NNPC, Nigeria, Dangote) instead of vague hooks.
Avoid overusing repetitive title formulas like starting every video with 'Exposed:'; it causes viewer fatigue and dilutes CTR.
For Shorts, lean into financial scandals with precise dollar/currency figures (e.g., '$11B Gas Scam', 'R2 Billion') as they drive higher retention.
Keep Short hooks under 3 seconds by jumping directly into the core event rather than intro context.
Rebrand the channel name to match the finance, corruption, and African business focus to build audience trust.
Produce more 3-8 minute long-form documentaries focusing on success stories (like Dangote) as watch time retention is surprisingly solid (44.5%).
double_down: South African state capture and banking collapses (Gupta Family, VBS Bank)
Profiles of prominent African billionaires and industrial empires (Aliko Dangote, Strive Masiyiwa, Mike Adenuga)
Specific high-stakes national economic stories with exact dollar amounts (Nigerian Naira evolution, NNPC oil revenue)
African tech unicorn breakdowns (Jumia, Flutterwave, Paystack)
avoid: Generic, repetitive title templates such as starting every title with 'Exposed:'
Vague titles lacking recognizable entity names (e.g., 'Exposed: The Oil Bribery Scam' or 'Exposed: $5B Looted From Central Bank')
Short-form titles that sound like generic stock news rather than narrative-driven stories
